summary: Ephemeral session fanout causing staggered 429s and missing Retry-After headers
description:
Issue summary:
Customer BrightCart reports intermittent 429 responses during their nightly catalog syncs that use multiplexed websocket sessions and very short-lived API keys (ephemeral tokens). The 429s arrive in waves across multiple clients with a ~30s stagger; some 429 responses include Retry-After headers, others do not.

Impact:
- BrightCart sync jobs fail to complete ~15% of the time during the nightly window (00:30-02:00 PST).
- Partial syncs lead to downstream inventory mismatch and customer-visible listing gaps.
- Engineering on-call requests clarity about whether this is configuration guidance or a bug in our accounting for ephemeral, multiplexed sessions.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool (dc-brightcart-ops) on prod in us-west-2
- Client uses websocket multiplexing over HTTP/2 with ephemeral keys rotated every 45s
- Traffic mix: 80% bulk embeddings and 20% small chat/generation calls used for telemetry

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Start 120 parallel websocket connections from 15 hosts using short-lived keys (rotate every 45s)
2) Each connection opens 8 multiplexed streams and issues periodic embed+generate calls at 10-20 qps per host
3) Observe 429 responses during the 00:30-02:00sync window; 429s arrive in groups with ~20-40s stagger

Observed behavior:
- 429s are not uniform; they come in sawtooth waves instead of a single capacity hit.
- Occasionally 429 responses lack Retry-After headers (client cannot back off deterministically).
- Console shows per-route burst pools allocated, but token-window metrics for the tenant show no single-shot drain.

Expected behavior:
- Throttling should be smooth and Retry-After consistently present for responses that are quota-driven.
- Dedicated pool should present predictable per-tenant accounting and clear headers for automated clients.

Logs / key headers (sanitized):
- Example 429 response with Retry-After: HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
  Retry-After: 60
  X-RateLimit-Tenant: 12000/12000
- Example 429 response without Retry-After: HTTP/2 429
  X-RateLimit-Tenant: 11986/12000
- Ingress proxy metrics show transient connection churn and a spike in auth-token-validation RPS coincident with rotations.

Workarounds attempted by customer:
- Increased ephemeral token TTL to 180s — reduced frequency of waves but did not eliminate 429s.
- Lowered parallel connections to 60 — bulk sync completed but with slower overall job runtime.

Requested outcome:
- Guidance on configuration best-practices for ephemeral key rotation + websocket multiplexing on Dedicated pools.
- Investigation into why Retry-After header is missing on a subset of 429s and whether this indicates accounting race between edge and origin.
- If a server-side fix is required, a timeline for mitigation or recommended temporary configs for BrightCart.

investigation_notes: Edge tracing shows token rotation events cause short-lived duplicate validation calls; duplicate calls may increment temporary counters before origin reconciliation completes.
Race window appears to be ~300-600ms during key swap; larger client fanout increases probability of staggered waves.
Inconsistent Retry-After likely due to 429 being returned by two different components: ingress (no header set in one codepath) vs origin (header set).
Priority to add header at ingress path and tighten atomicity of token-counter updates across proxies.
Related: SUP-412345 noted similar post-upgrade refill lag; lessons learned applied to trace selection.
next_steps: Push edge-proxy PR that ensures Retry-After header is set for ingress-returned 429s (PR #93 staged).
Instrument token-swap counter with per-connection token-hash logs for a 72h window to validate reduction in duplicate validation calls.
Work with BrightCart to trial TTL=120s + client-side jittered backoff as short-term mitigation.
If mitigation insufficient, schedule dedicated-pool rate-window smoothing configuration change to reduce burst sensitivity (follow-up change request).
resolution_notes: (pending) Canary PR merged to staging; awaiting 72h observation window on prod traces. Temporary mitigation recommended (TTL bump + client jitter). Will update ticket after observation window concludes.
